questions.q: What does Data Loader use to match each CSV row to an existing record during an Update?
options: The record's Name field automatically
The row number in the CSV
The record's Salesforce Id, which must be a column in the CSV
The date the record was created
questions.explain: Update requires an Id column so Data Loader knows exactly which record to change.

questions.q: Should your Insert CSV include an Id column?
options: No; Salesforce generates the Id for each new record
Yes; every insert must supply a unique Id
Yes, but only for custom objects
Only when the batch size is above 200
questions.explain: Ids are created by Salesforce on insert, so a new record's CSV row doesn't have one.

questions.q: In an Update, what happens to fields that are not mapped?
options: They are cleared to blank
They are deleted from the object
They cause the whole load to fail
They are left unchanged
questions.explain: Only the mapped columns are written; other fields keep their existing values.

questions.q: What are the success and error files that Data Loader writes after a load?
options: Backup copies of the original records
CSV files listing which rows succeeded and which failed, with the reason
Apex debug logs
Screenshots of the mapping screen
questions.explain: Data Loader writes a success file and an error file so you can confirm results and fix failed rows.

questions.q: What is a good habit before running a large Update?
options: Turn off field-level security for the whole org
Run it directly in Production with the full file
Export the affected records first, and test with a small file
Delete the records and re-insert them
questions.explain: A pre-change export gives you the original values, and a small test catches mapping mistakes cheaply.
